Charged Cartan Monte Carlo — v0.2 design: qudit-basis vertices¶

Status: implemented (opt-in via cfg.featureQuditBasis = True; cfg.featureChoiSigmaAB defaults to True once qudit basis is on) Builds on: v0.1 design — promotes the per-vertex Hilbert space from 2-dim (qubit) to 4-dim (ququart) Experiments: Experiment 02 (β-scan, the 4.6 plateau), Experiment 03 (finite-size T-scan, asymptote ≈ 4.07), Experiment 04 (Σ_AB Choi state, Q-conservation fix) Successor: v0.3 design — gauge mediation

Implementation note for the v0.2 promotion described in the v0.1 sketch. v0.2 makes charge intrinsic to the quantum state by promoting each vertex’s Hilbert space from a qubit (2-dim) to a ququart (4-dim) with the structure of a Dirac-spinor-like register:

basis = { |+0⟩, |+1⟩, |−0⟩, |−1⟩ }
        ── charge ──   ── spin ──

The first label is the charge sector (particle ↔ antiparticle); the second is the spin / internal qubit. The charge operator becomes

Q̂ = diag(+1, +1, −1, −1)

and the charge of a vertex is read out as ⟨q⟩_v = Tr[ρ_v · Q̂] ∈ [−1, +1]. Continuous charge values fall out of mixed states naturally; the classical chargeOf_ map is no longer needed.

What v0.2 fixes¶

The v0.1 model carries charge as a classical label chargeOf_[v] adjacent to the quantum state. This works but has structural limitations:

  • Q drifts under un-interact after annihilation (documented v0.1 limitation). The fix requires un-interact to know the history of charge modifications; with classical labels this is bookkeeping the model wasn’t designed to do.

  • No quantum charge superpositions. A vertex can be + or −, but not (|+⟩ + |−⟩)/√2. Real fermion-field charge eigenstates do admit such superpositions, and the matter-antimatter coherent oscillations that drive baryogenesis-like phenomena live in this subspace.

  • C and CP are imposed conventions, not symmetries. In v0.1 the CP-violating cpBias parameter biases pair-creation by hand. With charge intrinsic to the state, charge conjugation Ĉ = X_charge ⊗ I_spin becomes an operator on the Hilbert space, and CP-violation becomes “U doesn’t commute with Ĉ ⊗ P̂” — a structural statement about the chosen unitary, not an opt-in numerical knob.

Hilbert-space change¶

Matrix4cd (ququart, dim 4)

Numerical cost goes up roughly:

  • partialTrace: O(d²) → O(d⁴) ≈ 16×

  • Matrix multiplies in computeInteraction: 4×4 → 16×16 ≈ 64×

  • Per-cell wall time: estimated 30–50× slower than v0.1.

At our scale (T ~ 3000 cells, ~9000 vertices), that’s tractable.

Interaction unitary U¶

v0.2 needs a configurable 16×16 unitary on bipartite ququart inputs. Three options for parameterising it, in order of complexity:

  1. Direct Hamiltonian + exponentiate. Build a Hamiltonian on the bipartite ququart Hilbert space from a small number of physically- motivated terms, exponentiate via SelfAdjointEigenSolver:

    H_pair = J_c · (Q̂_A · Q̂_B)              ← charge-charge coupling
       + J_s · (σ^x_A·σ^x_B + σ^y_A·σ^y_B) ← spin-spin (XX + YY)
       + δ_m  · (Q̂_A + Q̂_B)              ← mass-like shift per charge
       + γ_CP · (Ĉ_A ⊗ I_B + I_A ⊗ Ĉ_B)   ← optional CP-violating term
U_pair = exp(−i · H_pair · dt)

    (J_c, J_s, δ_m, γ_CP, dt) are the configurable parameters. This is the path I’d take for v0.2 default.

  2. Operator Schmidt parameterisation. Pick the operator Schmidt spectrum (σ_k) and basis operators (A_k, B_k) directly — every 16×16 U has such a decomposition (the generalisation of the SU(4) Cartan core). More expressive but harder to motivate physically.

  3. Cartan / KAK on SU(16). Recursive decomposition into nested two-qubit blocks. Most general; most parameters; least illuminating physically. Defer.

We’ll go with (1) and use the operator Schmidt decomposition of the resulting U as a diagnostic at construction time (so we can report “how entangling is this choice of (J_c, J_s, …)” once and forget about it).

The Σ_AB-dimension mismatch¶

A worldline vertex carries a 4-dim ρ. The entangling core Σ_AB naturally carries the Choi state of U — a pure state on a 256-dim doubled Hilbert space. When Σ_AB later participates in an interaction with another vertex, we need to reduce its 256-dim state to something that fits into the standard 16-dim joint input.

v0.2 default: reduce-before-interaction (option A in the discussion). When Σ_AB is picked for interaction, partially trace its Choi state down to a 4-dim charge-basis subspace at the moment of interaction. The full Choi state is used at the moment of bowtie creation for principled per-edge MI calculation; the reduction only happens at subsequent consumption. This is the “interaction-as-measurement” reading: the partner vertex “measures” Σ_AB onto its charge eigenbasis.

Options B (promote-to-256-dim) and C (Σ_AB never interacts) remain deferred behind separate feature flags.

Move set under v0.2¶

Same four moves as v0.1 (interact, unInteract, annihilate, pairCreate), but their semantics simplify:

  • interact eligibility: opposite-sign pairs are not blocked at the eligibility filter (charge isn’t a separate label anymore). The interaction itself, applied to opposite-charge inputs, produces an output ρ_AB whose charge structure is whatever U dictates — including possible annihilation-like collapse if U happens to project onto the Q=0 subspace.

  • annihilate becomes a measurement move: pick a charged vertex, project its state onto the Q=0 sector with appropriate amplitude. This collapses the worldline (consistent with deactivation in v0.1.B) and the energy can optionally be carried away as a photon (v0.1.iii analog).

  • pairCreate spawns two vertices in a charge-entangled state: e.g. (|+,0⟩|−,0⟩ + |−,0⟩|+,0⟩)/√2 (Bell-like in the charge register, neutral spin). The CP-bias becomes asymmetry in the state coefficients, not in an external parameter.

  • unInteract: structurally identical to v0.1; the Q-drift bug disappears because charge is now propagated unitarily by U through the interaction, so un-interact (which removes the cell from the spacetime) automatically restores the pre-interact charge state.

Configuration¶

cfg.featureQuditBasis           = True   # turn on v0.2 (4-dim vertices)
cfg.j_chargeCharge              = 1.0    # H_pair: J_c
cfg.j_spinSpin                  = 0.25   # H_pair: J_s
cfg.massShift                   = 0.5    # H_pair: δ_m
cfg.gammaCpViolation            = 0.0    # H_pair: γ_CP (off by default)
cfg.dtPair                      = 0.25   # H_pair: dt

Old v0.1 flags (featureCharges, featureDeactivateOnAnnihilate, featurePhotonOnAnnihilate, cpBias) are ignored when featureQuditBasis is on (v0.2 supersedes them). The constructor reconciles this and warns if both are set.

Implementation order¶

  1. Foundation: introduce cfg.featureQuditBasis (default false); introduce a VertexDim runtime constant on the InteractionSimulation set at construction time (2 for v0.1, 4 for v0.2). All density-matrix buffers become Eigen::MatrixXcd with runtime size.

  2. Generalise the per-vertex / per-joint helpers: partialTrace, traceOutFirst/Second, tensor2, jointMutualInformation — they already use MatrixXcd internally for partialTrace; the typed 2-qubit versions get wrapped or replaced.

  3. Build the v0.2 Hamiltonian and U in schwingerTwoSiteU’s neighbourhood as quditPairU(J_c, J_s, delta_m, gamma_CP, dt).

  4. Re-port interact: read charges from Tr[ρ · Q̂] instead of chargeOf_; opposite-sign eligibility filter removed; charge inheritance becomes automatic via U.

  5. Re-port annihilate and pairCreate as measurement / pair-spawn on 4-dim states.

  6. Per-vertex observables: getGlobalCharge, getChargeProfile, getChargeCorrelation read from Tr[ρ · Q̂].

  7. Smoke test: confirm v0.1 path stays bit-identical at featureQuditBasis = false, then exercise v0.2 path end-to-end.

  8. β-scan and writeup comparable to v0.1’s.

Implementation status (initial pass)¶

✅ Done in the initial implementation:

  • featureQuditBasis flag wired into InteractionConfig; defaults to false (v0 backward compat preserved).

  • 4-dim per-vertex Hilbert space (quditStateOf_), 16-dim joint state buffer (quditJointOf_), 16×16 pair unitary (quditInteractionU_).

  • Charge operator Q̂ and charge-conjugation Ĉ defined; per-vertex charge derived as Tr[ρ · Q̂].

  • quditPairU(J_c, J_s, δ_m, γ_CP, dt) builds the canonical pair Hamiltonian and exponentiates it.

  • Initial layer projects each vertex into a definite ± charge sector (ALTERNATING by index or RANDOM).

  • interact builds the v0.2 result alongside the v0.1 result; uses the v0.2 edge MIs for the Regge action when the flag is on; seeds product states / joints into both buffers so observables stay consistent.

  • Σ_AB (entangling-core proxy) uses the maximally-mixed 4-dim state I/4, which is structurally neutral (⟨Q̂⟩ = 0), matching the v0.1 framing of AB as a neutral photon-like vertex.

  • getGlobalCharge reads Tr[ρ · Q̂] per frontier vertex under v0.2.

  • Python bindings expose the new flags and Hamiltonian parameters.

  • Test suite (tests/quantum/test_interaction_simulation_v02.cpp) with 6 checks, all passing: backward compat, sector projection, Q conservation at γ_CP=0, Q drift at γ_CP≠0, the v0.1 un-interact drift bug is fixed, peak D_S is a reasonable physical value.

🚧 Deferred to v0.3 (see v0.3.md which picks these up as preconditions for the gauge-mediation work):

  • annihilate / pairCreate measurement / spawn semantics in the qudit basis. The v0.1 moves still work (they read v0.1’s chargeOf_); under v0.2 they’re effectively no-ops because the v0.2 charge isn’t replicated into chargeOf_. The full v0.2 versions need to: project a charged vertex onto the Q = 0 subspace (annihilate); spawn a pair in a charge-entangled state (pairCreate).

  • getChargeProfile and getChargeCorrelation reading from qudit states via Tr[ρ · Q̂]. Under v0.2 they currently return zero / empty.

  • Σ_AB as the full 256-dim Choi state of U (currently the I/4 proxy).

These deferrals are bundled into v0.3 because v0.3’s gauge mediation needs the qudit-basis annihilate to produce real photons and the qudit-basis observables to characterise the resulting charge clustering. The first-pass v0.2 implementation already exercises the qudit Hilbert space end-to-end through the interact + tune + spectral-dim pipeline, which is what the v0.2 β-scan documents.

Open question for after implementation¶

The default H_pair is somewhat arbitrary — there are infinitely many ways to parameterise a 16×16 unitary, and the choice we make will affect every result. Two natural anchors:

  • Match v0.1 in a limit. Set J_c = 0 (no charge-charge coupling), keep J_s matching the v0.1 Schwinger fragment, and verify that v0.2 reproduces v0.1’s qualitative behaviour up to the inherent doubling. If it does, we have a clean baseline to add J_c ≠ 0 from.

  • Pick a known textbook coupled-fermion-pair model. The Nambu-Jona-Lasinio four-fermion interaction in 1+1D has exactly the right Hilbert-space structure (Dirac-spinor pairs) and a long experimental literature on chiral symmetry breaking. Mapping our (J_c, J_s, δ_m, γ_CP) to NJL parameters would tie the model to a known physics target.

I’d default to “match v0.1 in a limit” until results suggest pivoting.
